title: Flank Overload Through Rotation
content: A flank overload positions three or more attacking players on the same side of the pitch, creating a numerical superiority the defense cannot cover. The rotation involves central players shifting to overload one side while another player holds the opposite flank to prevent compression. Typical pattern: winger + fullback + central midfielder all arriving on the right flank creates a 3v2 against the opposing fullback and winger. The ball circulates quickly until a free player finds a crossing, cut-inside, or through ball opportunity. Key: the rotation must happen before the defense has time to shift — ball speed through the overloaded zone is critical.
